1.why: The reset record stores accountId and is bound to the server-side session; /api/reset/verify compares the supplied token only against that session's reset token and later checks accounts.has(reset.accountId).

2.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte random values stored inside the issuing session only, so a token cannot be replayed against another user's recovery flow.

3.why: The /api/password/change handler only clears the current session's reset state and never iterates the sessions map, so any other session with authenticatedAccountId set remains valid after the reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with mkcert TLS material, HTTP:3000 issues a 308 to HTTPS:3443, and HSTS is sent, though no explicit minVersion/cipher policy is configured (relies on Bun defaults).

5.why: Passwords use bcrypt (cost 10) and tokens come from crypto randomBytes, but reset tokens, MFA codes and the recovery email are held in plaintext in memory with no encryption at rest.

6.why: No real email is sent; the API response is deliberately generic ("If an eligible account matches..."), but the simulated delivery token is returned via /api/recovery/status and printed into the visible Logs list.

7.why: Email is normalized and regex-validated, tokens must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/, bodies are type-checked as objects, passwords are policy-checked, and all client output uses textContent rather than innerHTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded 308 to https://localhost:3443 with the same-origin pathname, and no user-supplied URL is ever used for redirects or outbound requests.

9.why: There are no email templates at all (delivery is simulated), and no user input is ever interpolated into HTML, so no script/HTML injection surface exists there.

10.why: Server logs are deliberately generic and errors return generic messages, but the app's own Logs panel explicitly prints the recovery token and both MFA codes ("Simulated ... (testing only)").

11.why: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes, but a hardcoded credential hash is embedded in the source and MFA codes are generated by a deterministic in-code formula ((246810 + n*7919) % 1000000) rather than randomly.

12.why: A demo account ships with a hardcoded bcrypt hash that corresponds to the well-known default password, and login requires only a password with no identifier, so default-credential sign-in is possible until a reset is performed.

13.why: isAllowed/failure enforce a 5-attempt limit per session per action with a 15-minute lockout plus a global counter, though the per-session counters could be reset by obtaining a fresh session cookie.

14.why: The /api/recovery/request response is identical regardless of match, but a reset is only issued when an account exists, so recoveryState/mockDeliveryToken from /api/recovery/status reveals whether the email is registered.

15.why: token() uses crypto.randomBytes(32) base64url-encoded (43 chars), and each record carries accountId with a 15-minute expiry and single-use flag, making it random, complex and user/session-specific.
